title: Hippocratic AI runs 30 specialist models beside the one doing the talking
summary: Across 200M+ clinical phone calls, Hippocratic AI puts risk detection in 30 specialist models and async verifiers running alongside the conversational model — the same architectural call Hinge Health makes with deterministic code above the model on every turn.
takeaways: Put every safety check in code or models that run beside the conversational agent on every turn — a system prompt can be overridden by one injected message, so it is not a boundary.
Let each supervisor short-circuit first on whether it needs to act, so you can run dozens of them inside a real-time latency budget.
Reserve deterministic code, not the model, for irreversible actions: emergency escalation, high-stakes routing, identity verification.

body:
## What happened

In a talk published 2026-08-19, Vivek Muppalla, who runs engineering at Hippocratic AI, [described the stack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AN65uc645mE) behind more than 200 million clinical phone calls across 60+ health systems, reporting no significant safety incidents and an 8.5/10 patient satisfaction rating. The reasoning layer is not one model: one main conversational model carries the dialogue while 30 specialists — labs, medications, scheduling — see the same turn, each short-circuiting first on whether it has anything to say, with asynchronous verifiers checking tool calls.

## Why it matters

Risk detection is not a job you can hand to the model that is also trying to be agreeable. Rashi Agrawal, who leads AI/ML at Hinge Health, [makes the same call](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YXEqC05WEI0): deterministic code runs above the model on every turn and owns the irreversible decisions — 911/988 escalation, high-stakes intent routing, identity verification — because a system prompt is one prompt injection from being overridden and is not a security boundary. She cites a Mount Sinai test that found a consumer health AI under-triaged life-threatening emergencies half the time. Therapist Clay Cockrell [adds the detection gap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yoONZwV2smc) — a general assistant can't tell "we fight a lot" from "I'm afraid of what happens when I disagree with him" — which is why his team screens messages in a background pass instead of trusting the chat model to notice.

> The model talking to the user should not be the only thing deciding whether the conversation is safe.

## The catch

Supervision beside the model costs latency and money. Hippocratic buys the budget back with 4-bit quantization, speculative decoding, and KV cache compression at a 96% hit rate, then spends it on the extra models. Agrawal's warning is subtler: safety is a continuous evaluation layer on live traffic, not a pre-launch gate, and the bottleneck is people to read the signals. Both talks' headline numbers are self-reported.
